question: How is molecular mass calculated?

options.text: By squaring atomic numbers of all elements
Adding all atomic masses of the atoms in molecule
Multiplying atomic radii of constituent elements
Adding all atomic volumes of the atoms present

solution:
The correct answer is __**Adding all atomic masses of the atoms in molecule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **molecular mass** of a compound is calculated by summing up the **atomic masses** of all the atoms present in its molecular formula. This involves identifying the number and type of atoms in the molecule and then adding their respective atomic masses.
 
• The **atomic mass** of an element is the weighted average mass of its isotopes, measured in atomic mass units (amu), and is available in the **periodic table**.
 
• For example, for water (H₂O):
 
 
• The atomic mass of hydrogen (H) is approximately 1 amu, and there are 2 hydrogen atoms in water.
 
• The atomic mass of oxygen (O) is approximately 16 amu, and there is 1 oxygen atom in water.
 
• The molecular mass = (2 × 1) + (1 × 16) = 18 amu.
